meta.titre: Kitchen Hygiene and Food Safety: Personal, Kitchen and Food Rules
meta.sous_theme: Four kinds of hygiene rule, contamination and food poisoning

source.epreuve_titre: GCE O/L Food and Nutrition past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A woman selling cooked rice and stew by a roadside near a motor park in Douala must keep the pots covered, wash her hands and keep flies away, or her customers may fall sick. Unsafe food can cause food poisoning, which is a serious cause of illness. This is why every GCE paper has questions on hygiene rules, on ways food is contaminated and on how to prevent it.

items: Bacteria are tiny living things; some of them are harmful and cause illness.
Soap and clean water remove dirt and many germs from hands.

sections.titre: Types of hygiene rule, contamination and food poisoning
sections.contenu_markdown:
### Four kinds of hygiene rule

| Kind | Meaning | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Personal hygiene | the cleanliness of the cook | wash hands with soap before cooking and after the toilet, touching raw meat or rubbish; cover the hair; clean apron; short clean nails; cover cuts with a waterproof plaster; never cough, sneeze or spit over food; do not cook when you have vomiting or diarrhoea |
| Kitchen hygiene | cleanliness of the place and equipment | clean worktops, sink and floor; wash up in hot soapy water and dry with a clean cloth; bins with lids, emptied daily; keep out flies, cockroaches and rats |
| Food hygiene | safe handling of food | keep raw and cooked food apart; cook thoroughly; cover food; refrigerate perishable food quickly; reheat leftovers thoroughly; wash fruit and vegetables |
| Food purchase hygiene | safe buying | buy from clean shops and stalls, check the dates and packaging, buy cold food last and take it home quickly |

### Contamination and food poisoning
**Contamination** means harmful organisms or substances get into food. It may be **biological** (bacteria, moulds), **physical** (hair, stones in rice or beans, glass) or **chemical** (insecticide, detergent). **Bacteria** multiply fastest in warm, moist food at temperatures near body temperature (about 37 °C). Thorough cooking kills most of them, a refrigerator slows their growth, and freezing stops their growth but does not reliably kill them.
**Food poisoning**, for example from Salmonella, shows as stomach pain, vomiting, diarrhoea and sometimes fever.

variantes.nom: Ways in which food is contaminated
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked for ways, sources or routes of contamination.

variantes.nom: Writing a list of hygiene rules
variantes.quand_utiliser: When asked to state or enumerate hygiene rules of one kind.
variantes.contenu_markdown: For a question like state or enumerate N hygiene rules, say which kind the question asks about, then give N different actions. A rule about the cook's body, clothes or habits is **personal hygiene**. Check that each point is an action, not a vague word such as "be clean".

sections.enonce_markdown: Enumerate five (5) ways of preventing flies from contaminating food in the kitchen. (5 marks)

etapes.action: Read the command word and the topic.
etapes.justification: Enumerate means list. The topic is preventing flies, so points must be actions that keep flies from food.
Flies land on refuse and dirt and carry germs on their feet and bodies to food.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Stop them reaching food and remove what attracts them.

etapes.action: Choose five separate ideas: covering, screening, waste, cleanliness, pest control.
etapes.justification: Each idea tackles the problem differently, so each earns a mark.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Covers; screens; bins with lids; cleaning spills; fly traps or insecticide away from food.

sections.conclusion_markdown: 1. Cover all food and keep it in covered containers. 2. Fit screens on the windows and doors of the kitchen. 3. Keep rubbish in bins with tight lids and empty them daily. 4. Wipe spills and crumbs at once and keep the kitchen and its surroundings clean. 5. Use fly traps or an insecticide safely, away from food and utensils.

items.erreur_markdown: Writing that hands are washed only after using the toilet.
items.pourquoi_faux: Hands must also be washed before starting to cook, after touching raw meat, after handling refuse and after coughing or sneezing into them.
items.correction_markdown: Wash hands with soap and clean water before and after handling food, and after the toilet and rubbish.

items.erreur_markdown: Cutting cooked meat on the board just used for raw chicken, with no washing in between.
items.pourquoi_faux: Germs move from the raw food to the cooked food (cross-contamination), and the cooked food will not be heated again to kill them.
items.correction_markdown: Use separate boards, or wash the board and knife in hot soapy water between raw and cooked foods.

items.erreur_markdown: Saying that freezing food kills all the bacteria in it.
items.pourquoi_faux: Freezing only stops bacteria from growing and does not reliably kill them; they can grow again when the food thaws. Thorough cooking is what kills them.
items.correction_markdown: Cooking kills most bacteria; the refrigerator slows them; the freezer stops them.

items.erreur_markdown: Listing the ways of contamination as: germs, bacteria, microbes, viruses, dirt.
items.pourquoi_faux: These are the agents of contamination, not the ways in which food is contaminated, so they score little.
items.correction_markdown: Write ways: dirty hands, flies, raw touching cooked food, dirty utensils, dirty water.

items.enonce_markdown: Say which kind of rule each one is (personal, kitchen, food or food purchase hygiene): (a) check the expiry date on a tin; (b) tie the hair back; (c) empty the bin every day; (d) cover leftovers and put them in the refrigerator.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **food purchase hygiene**; (b) **personal hygiene**; (c) **kitchen hygiene**; (d) **food hygiene**. (Award a mark for each.)

items.enonce_markdown: A woman sells cooked rice by the roadside. She leaves the pot uncovered all day, takes money and serves the rice with the same hands, and rinses the plates in one basin of water that is rarely changed. Identify four faults and say how each one should be corrected.
items.solution_markdown: Any four of: (1) pot uncovered, so flies and dust reach the food, so keep the pot covered; (2) handling money and food with the same hands, so wash hands or use a spoon and separate the person who takes money; (3) plates rinsed in a dirty basin, so wash them in hot soapy water, rinse in clean water and let them dry; (4) food kept for a long time in the warm air, so bacteria multiply, so keep the food hot or cook it in smaller quantities and reheat it thoroughly. (Award a mark for each fault with its correction, up to four.)

items.enonce_markdown: A cook cuts raw chicken on a board and then slices a tomato salad on the same board without washing it. Several guests develop vomiting and diarrhoea. (a) Name the process by which the salad was contaminated. (b) Explain why the salad is more dangerous than the chicken in this case. (c) State three steps that would have prevented the illness.
items.solution_markdown: (a) **Cross-contamination**: bacteria from the raw chicken passed to the salad through the board. (b) The chicken will be cooked, which kills bacteria. The salad is eaten raw, so any bacteria that reach it survive and multiply. (c) Any three of: use a separate board and knife for raw meat; wash the board and knife in hot soapy water between jobs; wash hands after touching raw chicken; prepare salad first or store it covered in a refrigerator; cook the chicken thoroughly.

items_markdown: There are four kinds of hygiene rule: personal, kitchen, food and food purchase hygiene; classify a rule by who or what it concerns.
Personal hygiene: wash hands, cover hair, clean apron, short nails, cover cuts, never cough or sneeze over food.
Contamination can be biological, physical or chemical; give ways such as dirty hands, flies, cross-contamination and dirty water.
Cooking kills most bacteria; the refrigerator slows them down; freezing does not kill them.
Answer enumerate and state questions with the exact number of different action points.
